evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict-of-law rules.
evidence.rationale: Section 16.1 selects California law.

evidence.quote: The parties agree in writing that Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner fixes the time when Contractor's payment to Subcontractor becomes due.
evidence.rationale: Section 5.2 is titled Pay When Paid. Owner payment fixes the timing of payment. It is not stated as a condition precedent to the obligation to pay.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner
evidence.rationale: Section 5.2 sets payment at 7 days after Contractor receives Owner payment.

evidence.quote: The parties agree in writing that Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner fixes the time when Contractor's payment to Subcontractor becomes due.
evidence.rationale: A specific 7-day period is written into Section 5.2.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall withhold retainage of five percent (5%) from each progress payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: 5% retainage equals 500 basis points.

release_condition.value: Retainage becomes payable upon both (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner covering the Subcontract Work.

evidence.quote: Retainage becomes payable upon both (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner covering the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states both release conditions. Section 7.3 adds closeout deliverables required before release.

evidence.quote: release retainage to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 requires release within 10 days after the triggers.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1 requires a conditional waiver with each application.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment for the amount received.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2 requires an unconditional waiver after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall also deliver conditional and unconditional waivers, in the same statutory forms, from each of its sub-subcontractors and material suppliers whose labor or materials are included in that application.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4 requires lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136 and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.3 requires the California statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due to Subcontractor, including retainage, the amount of any backcharge for costs Contractor incurs because of Subcontractor's failure to perform under this Subcontract.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1 grants a backcharge setoff right.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount sufficient to cover the cost of correcting defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work until that work is corrected and accepted.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2 permits withholding for defective work.

evidence.quote: Contractor may include in a progress payment the value of materials and equipment delivered to the Project site and suitably stored there for later incorporation into the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: On-site stored materials may be paid if protected and invoiced. Off-site materials are payable only with Contractor's prior written approval, proof of insurance and a bill of sale (Section 6.2). Both on-site and off-site payment are conditional.

anomalies.description: Off-site stored materials are payable only with Contractor's prior written approval, which is discretionary. Payment also requires insurance naming Contractor and Owner as loss payees and a bill of sale transferring title.

evidence.quote: Materials stored off site are payable only with Contractor's prior written approval, proof of insurance, and a bill of sale transferring title.
evidence.rationale: Off-site stored materials are payable only with Contractor's prior written approval, which is discretionary. Payment also requires insurance naming Contractor and Owner as loss payees and a bill of sale transferring title.

anomalies.description: Approval for off-site storage is limited to each shipment or location and does not carry over to other shipments or locations.

evidence.quote: Approval for one shipment or storage location does not extend to any other.
evidence.rationale: Approval for off-site storage is limited to each shipment or location and does not carry over to other shipments or locations.

anomalies.description: On-site stored materials payment is permissive ('may include') and conditioned on protection and separate listing with invoices.

evidence.quote: This applies only if the materials are protected from weather, theft and damage and are listed separately in the application for payment with supporting invoices.
evidence.rationale: On-site stored materials payment is permissive ('may include') and conditioned on protection and separate listing with invoices.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release also depends on Final Completion, which includes acceptance by Owner's representative. Further closeout deliverables are required before release.

evidence.quote: Before retainage is released, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor:
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release also depends on Final Completion, which includes acceptance by Owner's representative. Further closeout deliverables are required before release.

anomalies.description: The setoff right extends to retainage.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due to Subcontractor, including retainage
evidence.rationale: The setoff right extends to retainage.

anomalies.description: Contractor may withhold the next progress payment until it receives the unconditional waiver for the prior payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold the next payment until it receives the unconditional waiver.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold the next progress payment until it receives the unconditional waiver for the prior payment.

anomalies.description: Termination-for-convenience payments are conditioned on Contractor's recovery from Owner, which is pay-if-paid style language outside the progress payment clause.

evidence.quote: These payments are made only to the extent Contractor recovers them from Owner, and no payment shall be made for anticipated profit on unperformed work.
evidence.rationale: Termination-for-convenience payments are conditioned on Contractor's recovery from Owner, which is pay-if-paid style language outside the progress payment clause.

anomalies.description: Delay compensation and time extensions are limited to relief Contractor obtains from Owner.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall be entitled to an extension of time or additional compensation for delay only to the extent Contractor obtains corresponding relief from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Delay compensation and time extensions are limited to relief Contractor obtains from Owner.

anomalies.description: A broad discretionary withholding right is based on Contractor's belief that the remaining balance is insufficient to complete the work.

evidence.quote: a reasonable belief that the remaining balance of the Subcontract Sum will not be enough to complete the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: A broad discretionary withholding right is based on Contractor's belief that the remaining balance is insufficient to complete the work.

anomalies.description: Contractor may unilaterally adjust payment applications based on its own evaluation before submitting them to Owner.

evidence.quote: Contractor may adjust an application to reflect its good-faith evaluation of the work actually completed
evidence.rationale: Contractor may unilaterally adjust payment applications based on its own evaluation before submitting them to Owner.
